item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
King’s Lynn man jailed for shoplifting
A 39-year-old man from Gaywood has been sentenced to 12 weeks in prison after admitting to multiple thefts from a King’s Lynn supermarket. Shane Davis Wilson, of Pleasance Close, targeted the Heron Foods store in the town centre on three occasions in September. The court heard that he stole items including steak, wine, and sweets.
Magistrates were told the defendant had breached a previous suspended sentence. In addition to the jail term, Davis Wilson has been ordered to pay £104.17 in compensation to the store. His defence solicitor stated that the thefts were committed due to financial difficulties and hunger.

item.description:

Heacham pupils join Shakespeare performances in King’s Lynn
Pupils from Heacham Junior School have taken part in the annual Robert Armin Festival at King’s Lynn Minster. Twenty-six Year 6 students attended the event to watch comedic adaptations of A Midsummer Night’s Dream and Romeo and Juliet, performed by 440 Theatre.
During the productions, students and staff were invited to join the actors on stage. Assistant head teacher Ashley Kirwan participated in a scene from Romeo and Juliet, while teaching assistant Charlotte Guest also accompanied the group. Mr Kirwan noted that the festival’s humorous approach helps make Shakespeare’s work more accessible to young people, while strengthening their connection to the local history of the Elizabethan actor Robert Armin.

item.title: King’s Lynn man fined after breaching town centre ban
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
King’s Lynn man fined after breaching town centre ban
A prolific offender from King’s Lynn has been fined after failing to comply with a community protection notice. Twenty-nine-year-old Levi Coburn, of Anthony Nolan Road, appeared at Lynn Magistrates’ Court on Thursday. He admitted to breaching an order that bans him from entering the town centre.
The court heard that on September 2, Coburn refused to leave the town’s bus station when instructed by police. He shouted at officers while they were speaking with another individual. In mitigation, the court was told that Coburn was intoxicated at the time. He has been ordered to pay a total of £190, consisting of a £100 fine, a £40 victim surcharge, and £50 in court costs.
